first registration's held-out leg came back VOID and its cross-check leg

WHAT HAPPENED TO THE FIRST ONE, stated here so this file is readable on its
own (full numbers in line-edge-priority-order.json and in the investigation):

  LEG 1 -- HELD-OUT PRIORITY: **VOID**. Line_0003.0 - Line_0007.0 yield NINE
  decisive pixels between them, against the 200 the registration named as the
  validity floor. At widths 3-7 the primitives' wide edges barely overlap and
  the 3px margin removes what little core is left. The leg was registered with
  that escape written into it, and it is being called void rather than passed:
  all eight order schemes score 100% on nine pixels, which is not evidence.

  LEG 2 -- HELD-OUT EXTENT: **PASS, and non-discriminating exactly as
  registered**. w(1+tan/2) is in-band on 100.0% of 4,445 clean samples over 39
  edges at widths 3-5 -- but the perpendicular rectangle manages 98.16% there,
  because at those widths the two models differ by well under a pixel. The
  registration said in advance this leg could only catch a blunder. It caught
  none. The discrimination is the fit set's >= 2px subset: 100% against 0%.

  LEG 3 -- THE TWO RULES EXPLAINING EACH OTHER: **FAIL**. Rebuilding the
  candidate footprints with the derived extent rule was predicted to raise
  opp_abc to at least 99.3% and to raise it on each of five blocks. It rose to
  98.97% (from 98.73%) and rose on four of five -- Tri 98.05 -> 98.27, QStrip
  98.78 -> 98.89, LLoop 98.61 -> 99.24, Poly 99.34 -> 99.47 -- and FELL on
  Quad, 99.66 -> 99.60. Direction right, magnitude wrong, one block against.
  So roughly 1% of decisive pixels are not accounted for by the wrong-footprint
  story, and that 1% is the most honest open question here.

=== THIS REGISTRATION ===

docs/testing/line_priority.py --reconstruct renders the whole scene with a
painter's algorithm under each of the eight order schemes crossed with both
extent rules, and scores every interior ink pixel against the golden. It
applies NO pixel selection: no colour-separation threshold, no requirement
that the golden match some candidate, no multi-coverage requirement. That is
the point -- it is the measurement a rule fitted to the decisive pixels could
fail.

Known context, and it is not a prediction: the smoke run at w = 16 alone gives
opp_abc + hypot-approx 99.25% within 16/255 over 34,002 pixels, against
ours + perp rect 93.34%. w = 16 is in the fit set.

LEG 5a -- HELD OUT, widths 3.0 to 7.0, five captures never scored by anything.
  --min-width 3 --max-width 7 --reconstruct
PREDICTED: opp_abc + hypot-approx is the top-ranked of the sixteen
combinations, and scores at least 90% within 16/255.
  REGISTERED CAVEAT, before the numbers: at these widths almost no ink is in an
  overlap, so every order scheme will score similarly and the SPREAD will be
  small. I am predicting the RANKING and a floor, not a gap, and if the spread
  is under half a point I will report the leg as non-discriminating rather than
  claim it. What it can still catch is a rule that is right on wide overlaps
  and wrong about the scene.
  FAILS IF: any other combination outranks it, or it falls below 90%.

LEG 5b -- THE WHOLE CORPUS, widths 3 to 64.875.
  --min-width 3 --reconstruct
PREDICTED, all four together:
  (1) opp_abc + hypot-approx is the top-ranked of the sixteen combinations;
  (2) it scores at least 95% within 16/255;
  (3) ours + perp rect -- what this emulator draws today for QUADS, QUAD_STRIP
      and POLYGON -- scores at least 4 percentage points lower;
  (4) for EVERY one of the eight order schemes, hypot-approx extent scores
      higher than perp rect extent. This is the part that is not about
      priority at all: it says the extent rule is independent of the order
      rule, and it is four-teen separate comparisons that could each go the
      other way.
  FAILS IF: any of the four does not hold. (3) is the one most able to fail
  benignly -- most of the scene's ink is not in an overlap, so a 4-point gap is
  a real demand rather than a formality. (1) and (4) are the ones that would
  actually hurt: (1) failing would mean the decisive-pixel derivation does not
  generalise to the scene, and (4) failing would mean the extent rule is an
  artefact of the order rule I happened to pair it with.

WHAT I STILL DO NOT PREDICT: any pixel total for any renderer change; the cap
shape; the floor/ceil phase; anything about the sub-2px widths; and anything
about TRIANGLE_STRIP, which `Line width` does not draw and whose (a,b,c)
labelling alternates with winding, so the rule's application to it is inferred
rather than measured.
